UNH.rationale: UNH is a high-quality franchise with dominant market positions (30% Medicare Advantage share, largest commercial insurer) and strong cash generation ($8.91B Q1 2026 OCF, +63.3% YoY). However, the stock is priced for growth that the numbers do not deliver. YoY EPS growth is just +0.7% ($6.90 vs $6.85) despite +2.0% revenue growth, indicating margin compression. ROE has collapsed from 22.8% to 12.3% and net margin has halved from 5.6% to 2.8% — the market is paying peak multiples for trough profitability. PE diluted has expanded from 12.0x to 30.7x (at the 52-week ceiling) while earnings are essentially flat. The earnings yield of 3.3% is below the 3-month Treasury yield (3.83%) and 10-year Treasury yield (4.54%), creating a persistent valuation headwind. Price has surged +41.1% in one quarter against -1.3% QoQ revenue growth — a classic valuation overshoot. Multiple unresolved regulatory actions (DOJ billing investigation, FTC insulin pricing settlement, prior-authorization scrutiny) create additional downside risk. Berkshire Hathaway's exit of its entire 3.3M-share stake signals institutional caution. The July 16 earnings report is a near-term catalyst, but even a beat (Bernstein projects $5.22 vs $4.84 consensus) may not be enough to justify a 30.7x PE on flat earnings. Mean reversion of the multiple to even 15-18x would imply 40-50% price risk without any earnings deterioration.
